answers.answer: Open Economy in the sidebar and choose the Leaderboards tab. Choose New leaderboard and the New leaderboard dialog opens. Pick Ranks by, Period, Over, Places shown and Visible to viewers, then choose Save leaderboard. The dialog closes and the leaderboard shows in the list. To show the ranking, a viewer types !leaderboard in chat. The bot answers with the top 5 of the first leaderboard in the list that has Visible to viewers on.
answers.quote: Open Economy in the sidebar and choose the Leaderboards tab.

answers.answer: You need the Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster role. Without it the Leaderboards tab is hidden. This is stated under Who can use this. Under Before you add one, the page says chat shows only one leaderboard, chosen by list order. It also says a One jar board needs a jar your channel owns or has an accepted membership in.
answers.quote: By default, a Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster may see, add, change and delete leaderboards.

answers.answer: In the dashboard, success means the dialog closes and the leaderboard shows in the list. Each row reads like Whole channel · All time · top 10, and a hidden board carries the Private badge. In chat, the bot replies with each rank, the viewer's Twitch ID and the amount. Balance ranks what a viewer holds now. Earned and Spent rank activity during the period.
answers.quote: The dialog closes and the leaderboard shows in the list.

answers.answer: Add a board with Ranks by set to Earned, Period set to Weekly and Over set to Whole channel. It ranks currency gained since midnight UTC on the most recent Sunday, not the saved balances. For !leaderboard to show it, no visible Balance board can exist, because Balance comes first in the list. So you turn Visible to viewers off on any Balance board.
answers.quote: For example, a Whole channel, Earned, Weekly board ranks currency earned since Sunday, not the largest long-term balance.

answers.answer: I learned only after the add steps that chat always shows the top 5, whatever Places shown says. The cost is that a reader may set Places shown expecting it to change the chat reply, then has to reread. The list-order rule is stated before the steps, so I did not have to guess at that one.
answers.quote: The bot answers with the top 5 viewers of the leaderboard chosen as described in Before you add one, whatever Places shown says.

answers.answer: Read aloud, the example row with its middle dots is awkward, because a listener hears the separators or nothing at all. The cost is small. Otherwise the page reads cleanly and does not explain what a leaderboard is for in general.

warning_review.reason: A word count alone is not a defect. This is a reference page with two tables, the reader found all six answers, and the cost is reading time only, so the wording stands.
The 188 words before the steps are access and consequence facts: who sees the tab, the list-order rule and the One jar membership need. Voice rule 4 puts these before the steps, so the order stays.
The sentence is dense, but it is the list-order rule the reader needs before adding a board, and blind answers 2 and 4 used it. Splitting it would add no information, so it stays.
The sentence states a surprise the reader must know before changing a board: turning Visible to viewers off does not by itself keep every ranking out of chat. It comes before the steps, so it stays.
